introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (0575). Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen; answer any two questions). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae Booklets may be used.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A car accelerates at $2\,\text{m s}^{-2}$ uniformly from rest for 3 seconds.

(a) Find the speed of the car at this instant. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $v=u+at$ with $u=0$, $a=2\,\text{m s}^{-2}$, $t=3$ s:

$$v=0+2\times3=6.$$

**The speed of the car is $6\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
It maintains this speed for the next 5 seconds and then decelerates uniformly to rest for the next 3 seconds.

(b) Draw a velocity-time graph to illustrate the motion of the car. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The motion has three stages, so the graph has three straight segments (time $t$ in seconds on the horizontal axis, velocity $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ on the vertical axis):

| Stage | Time interval | Velocity | Segment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acceleration | $0\le t\le3$ | from $0$ to $6$ | straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(3,6)$ |
| Constant speed | $3\le t\le8$ | $6$ | horizontal line from $(3,6)$ to $(8,6)$ |
| Deceleration | $8\le t\le11$ | from $6$ to $0$ | straight line from $(8,6)$ to $(11,0)$ |

The graph is a trapezium: it rises from the origin to $(3,6)$, stays level to $(8,6)$, then falls to $(11,0)$ on the $t$-axis. Label the axes with units and mark the points $3$, $8$, $11$ and the value $6$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
From the graph or otherwise,

(c) find the total distance travelled by the car. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The distance is the area under the velocity-time graph, a trapezium with parallel sides $5$ (top, from $t=3$ to $t=8$) and $11$ (base, from $t=0$ to $t=11$) and height $6$:

$$\text{distance}=\frac12(5+11)\times6=48.$$

(Check by stages: $\frac12(3)(6)+5(6)+\frac12(3)(6)=9+30+9=48$.)

**Total distance $=48$ m.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A particle, P, of mass 3 kg is connected by a light inextensible string, which passes over a smooth fixed pulley to a particle Q of mass 4 kg, hanging freely. The string is held taut and the particles are released from rest.

Find:

(a) the common acceleration of the particles, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Model used: both particles hang vertically on either side of the pulley (no figure is given); $g=10\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.* Q is the heavier, so Q moves down and P moves up with the same acceleration $a$ (inextensible string) and the same tension $T$ (smooth pulley, light string).

- Q (downwards): $4g-T=4a$
- P (upwards): $T-3g=3a$

Adding: $g=7a$, so

$$a=\frac{g}{7}=\frac{10}{7}\approx1.43.$$

**The common acceleration is $\dfrac{10}{7}\approx1.43\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the tension in the string, *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the equation for P: $T=3g+3a=3(10)+3\cdot\dfrac{10}{7}=30+\dfrac{30}{7}=\dfrac{240}{7}$.

(Check with Q: $T=4g-4a=40-\dfrac{40}{7}=\dfrac{240}{7}$.)

**The tension is $\dfrac{240}{7}\approx34.3$ N.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the force exerted on the pulley. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The string pulls the pulley with a force $T$ on each side, both acting vertically downwards, so the force on the pulley is

$$2T=\frac{480}{7}\approx68.6.$$

**The force exerted on the pulley is $\dfrac{480}{7}\approx68.6$ N, directed vertically downwards.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) A particle, P of mass 3 kg moves on a straight line with speed $4\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and collides with a stationary particle Q, of mass 2 kg. After collision P moves with speed $2\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

Find,

(a) the speed of Q after collision, *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
P keeps moving in its original direction after the impact. Conservation of linear momentum along the line:

$$3(4)+2(0)=3(2)+2v\ \Longrightarrow\ 12=6+2v\ \Longrightarrow\ v=3.$$

**The speed of Q after the collision is $3\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the loss in kinetic energy. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy before: $\frac12(3)(4)^2+0=24$ J.

Kinetic energy after: $\frac12(3)(2)^2+\frac12(2)(3)^2=6+9=15$ J.

$$\text{loss}=24-15=9\text{ J}.$$

**The loss in kinetic energy is $9$ J.**
